title: Clamp a Number
prompt: A slider control must keep values inside its allowed range. Write a function that returns the value if it is between min and max, min if it is too low, and max if it is too high.

explanation.beginner:
Example: clampNumber(5, 0, 10) produces 5. Apply both bounds so values inside the interval remain unchanged and outliers move to the nearest permitted bound.

Compare “clamps low values”: input [-4,0,10] produces 0. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Apply both bounds so values inside the interval remain unchanged and outliers move to the nearest permitted bound.

Tempting mistake: A check for only one boundary leaves the other side invalid. Include exact boundaries in the examples.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “clamps low values”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
